extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency officials responsible for standards policy and implementation (Standards Executives, agency heads, procurement and regulatory staff, NIST/OMB liaisons)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reporting requirements for Federal agencies to prefer and manage voluntary consensus standards, coordinate participation in standards bodies, and report uses of government-unique standards under OMB Circular A-119 and the NTTAA. Covers solicitation procedures, agency responsibilities, standards-management systems, and interagency coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a centralized standards management system
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a centralized standards management system that identifies how your agency uses both government-unique and voluntary consensus standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This system is required for agencies that use government-unique standards frequently or are involved in long-term procurements requiring government-unique replacement parts. The centralized system supports either categorical or transaction-based reporting and tracking of agencies' standards use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic review for conversion to voluntary standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically review your agency’s use of government-unique standards for conversion to voluntary consensus standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must periodically evaluate whether government-unique standards can be replaced by voluntary consensus standards and plan for conversion where feasible to promote economy and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain records and explanations for using government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records on the groups or categories in which your agency uses government-unique standards in lieu of voluntary consensus standards, including an explanation of the reasons for such use, which must be transmitted according to Section 9a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records should document rationale (e.g., legal inconsistency, impracticality) whenever government-unique standards are used instead of voluntary consensus standards; these records feed agency reports to OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable offerors to suggest alternative voluntary standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable potential offerors to suggest voluntary consensus standards that can replace government-unique standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide mechanisms (e.g., in solicitations) for offerors to propose alternative voluntary standards that meet agency requirements, facilitating substitution where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transaction-based reporting when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on a transaction basis when your agency identifies, manages, and reviews the use of standards on a transaction basis rather than a category basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transaction-based reporting is useful when procurement is mostly commercial but occasionally involves government-unique standards. Follow the solicitation-level procedures specified for transaction reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation must identify government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: In each solicitation which references government-unique standards, the solicitation must identify such standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When government-unique standards are cited in solicitations, they must be explicitly identified to ensure transparency and to allow offerors to propose alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation must allow offerors to suggest alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: In each solicitation referencing government-unique standards, provide potential offerors an opportunity to suggest alternative voluntary consensus standards that meet the agency’s requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural requirement tied to transaction-based reporting; agencies should give a clear mechanism and timeframe for submitting suggested alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify use of government-unique standards in reports
rubrics_metrics.description: If suggestions are made and the agency decides to use government-unique standards in lieu of voluntary consensus standards, the agency must explain in its report to OMB why using such voluntary consensus standards is inconsistent with applicable law or otherwise impractical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must document and transmit these explanations according to Section 9a; reasons must show legal inconsistency or impracticality to justify non-substitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: COTS and voluntary/non-consensus private-sector exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: For solicitations for commercial-off-the-shelf products (COTS), or for products or services that rely on voluntary consensus standards or non-consensus standards developed in the private sector, or for products that otherwise do not rely on government-unique standards, the requirements in this section do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may treat COTS and products already relying on voluntary/private standards as outside the government-unique/solicitation-notice requirements; document applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of Commerce: coordinate and provide guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of Commerce coordinates and fosters executive branch implementation of this Circular and, as appropriate, provides administrative guidance to assist agencies in implementing this Circular including guidance on identifying voluntary consensus standards bodies and voluntary consensus standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary also sponsors/supports the ICSP, reports to OMB on implementation, establishes procedures for agency directories, and issues guidance on conformity assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor and support the Interagency Committee on Standards Policy (ICSP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor and support the Interagency Committee on Standards Policy (ICSP), chaired by NIST, which considers agency views and advises the Secretary and agency heads on the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIST provides chair and secretariat for the ICSP; ICSP uses working groups to address targeted issues (e.g., ISO 9000/14000, lab accreditation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary to report to OMB on implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of Commerce reports to the Director of OMB concerning the implementation of the policy provisions of this Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures OMB oversight of executive-branch compliance and effectiveness of implementation across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish procedures for agency directories and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish procedures for agencies to use when developing directories described in Section 15b(5) and establish procedures to make these directories available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directories identify agency employees participating in voluntary standards bodies; agencies are encouraged to publish/make directories available (including via Internet).

rubrics_metrics.name: Heads of Agencies: implement and ensure compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Heads of Agencies implement the policies of this Circular in accordance with procedures described and ensure agency compliance with the policies of the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an agency has significant interest in standards, the head must designate a senior Standards Executive and ensure annual reports are transmitted as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and reporting by Standards Executive
rubrics_metrics.description: In agencies with significant interest in standards, designate a senior-level official as the Standards Executive responsible for implementing this Circular and representing the agency on the ICSP; transmit the annual report prepared by the Agency Standards Executive as described in Sections 9 and 15b(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards Executives are the focal point for agency standards policy, reporting, and interagency coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards Executive: promote clear, consistent agency positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote development of agency positions that are in the public interest, do not conflict with each other, are consistent with administration policy, and are clearly defined and known in advance to all federal participants on a given committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes ensuring positions reflect agency missions and are available to agency participants prior to standards-body meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish procedures to coordinate representatives' views
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish procedures to ensure that agency representatives who participate in voluntary consensus standards bodies will, to the extent possible, ascertain the views of the agency and will, at a minimum, express views that are not inconsistent or in conflict with established agency views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should include preparation of agency views, coordination with other agencies when multiple agencies participate, and internal sign-off processes as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure participation consistent with agency mission and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent possible, ensure that the agency’s participation in voluntary consensus standards bodies is consistent with agency missions, authorities, priorities, and budget resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should prioritize standards activities that align with strategic needs and available resources; Standards Executives should plan staff and resource allocation accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate interagency positions to present unified views
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more agencies participate in a given voluntary consensus standards activity, ensure they coordinate their views on matters of paramount importance so as to present, whenever feasible, a single, unified position and, where not feasible, a mutual recognition of differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination mitigates conflicting federal input; ICSP and Standards Executives should facilitate unified positions where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperate with the Secretary in implementing the Circular
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperate with the Secretary of Commerce in carrying out his or her responsibilities under this Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes consulting with the Secretary as needed on internal procedures, guidance, and agency directories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult with Secretary on internal procedures and directories
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult with the Secretary, as necessary, in the development and issuance of internal agency procedures and guidance implementing this Circular, including development and implementation of an agency-wide directory identifying agency employees participating in voluntary consensus standards bodies and the identification of voluntary consensus standards bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation ensures consistency across agencies and supports the creation of harmonized directories and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and submit reports on use of government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare, as described in Section 9, a report on uses of government-unique standards in lieu of voluntary consensus standards and a report on the status of agency standards policy activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should include numbers of participants, voluntary standards used and substituted, government-unique standards used, and explanations for non-substitution; submit annually to NIST/OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish ongoing review process of agency standards use
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing a process for ongoing review of the agency’s use of standards for purposes of updating such use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should periodically review and update which standards they reference or require, replacing government-unique standards with voluntary ones where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with budget and legal offices for participation review
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate with appropriate agency offices (e.g., budget and legal offices) to ensure that effective processes exist for the review of proposed agency support for, and participation in, voluntary consensus standards bodies, so that agency support and participation will comply with applicable laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal and budget reviews should be integrated into decisions to support or participate in standards bodies to avoid ethics or statutory conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ICSP working groups and NIST support for technical issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ICSP working groups (e.g., ISO 9000, ISO 14000, laboratory accreditation, directory/database, standards management) and NIST support to address agency technical and policy-related standards activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working groups provide forums for focused issues, sharing best practices and developing guides (e.g., Quality Management Systems Guide).

rubrics_metrics.name: Track participation and adoption metrics for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve and utilize systems for tracking the adoption or referencing of voluntary standards, as well as the level of staff participation in voluntary standards-developing bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should collect and report metrics (e.g., number of participating employees, standards used/substituted, government-unique standards in use) and use electronic directories/databases for collection and exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop agency policy/program elements to support implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop specific policy and programmatic elements to support the implementation of the NTTAA and OMB Circular A-119 (e.g., agency standards policy units, monitoring, resource allocation, infrastructure, reporting, program effectiveness assessment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider recommendations (e.g., per ICF Kaiser report) for structuring agency support functions, monitoring, and evaluation of standards activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan participation according to strategic agency needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider agency strategic needs when planning for agency participation in standards activities; use available resources including NIST to determine applicable Standards Developing Organizations (SDOs), relevant voluntary standards, and the need for new standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize standards participation that meets future agency and national needs; avoid overcommitment and focus on relevant committees and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICSP to develop participant-preparation guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICSP should develop guidelines for use when agencies prepare staff for participation in standards-related activities, reflecting the need to prepare agency views and coordinate positions, avoid appearance of dominance, and consider likely future agency and national needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines should include preparation of coordinated positions, ethical considerations, and training/materials (examples and lessons learned exist, such as GIQLP supporting materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use electronic means and directories for information exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Use electronic means for setting up directory databases of participants and exchanging information about standards-related issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are encouraged to publish directories and supporting materials on the Internet to facilitate access and interagency coordination; questionnaire results indicate many agencies already use or plan Internet directories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and report trends in Federal participation and adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and report data on the number of Federal employees participating in voluntary standards bodies, voluntary standards used, voluntary standards substituted for government-unique standards, and the number of government-unique standards used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metrics (as shown in Table 1) are used to evaluate effectiveness of policy implementation and to identify declines or increases in participation that may warrant action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer voluntary consensus standards except when disadvantages exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal policy: rely on voluntary standards whenever feasible and consistent with law and regulation, and give preference to voluntary standards over non-mandatory government standards unless use would adversely affect performance or cost, reduce competition, or have other significant disadvantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy objective is greater economy and efficiency; agencies must document and justify exceptions where voluntary standards are not used.
